newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cabinet names new secret service head.
newsitem.headline: Czech cabinet names new secret service head.

text.p: The Czech cabinet decided on Wednesday to appoint Karel Vulterin, a scientist, as head of the secret service to replace Stanislav Devaty, who quit in a political row last November.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news conference that the cabinet unanimously agreed to name Vulterin as director of the Security Information Service (BIS).
Devaty, a controversial protege of Klaus, resigned after allegations that the BIS had spied on Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux and then tried to cover up its actions.
The row led to a public squabble between the Christian Democrats, a junior coalition partner led by Lux, and Klaus, who heads the conservative Civic Democratic Party (ODS).

Minister without portfolio Pavel Bratinka, who oversees the secret service, told private television station TV Nova that Vulterin was chosen because he was outside the Czech security structure and had no ties to political parties.
Vulterin is currently the head of a university scientific laboratory in Prague studying radio isotopes.
